h1: What are the tree replacement and mitigation payment rules in Newton, MA?
title: Newton Tree Replacement Rules: Replacement Inches and Payments
description: Understand how Newton calculates replacement planting and when an applicant may make a payment instead of planting replacement trees.
short_answer: Newton's Tree Preservation Ordinance uses replacement inches based on the diameter of the removed tree. The City allows an applicant to plant replacement trees, make a payment in lieu of planting, or use a combination. The exact payment amount must be confirmed from the current City schedule; it should not be estimated from replacement inches alone.

facts.text: Newton's replacement table bases the required replacement inches on the size of the removed tree. Its examples show that a 14-inch tree requires 14 replacement inches and a 26-inch tree requires 39 replacement inches.
Newton allows an applicant to make a payment to the City in lieu of planting replacement trees, or to combine planting and payment.

qa.q: Is the replacement requirement always one inch planted for each inch removed?
qa.a: No. Newton's replacement table increases the required replacement inches for larger trees, so the calculation is not always one-for-one.
